# SPD-096 — A real parked bucket on the board

## Brief
## Why

There is no backlog status. Tickets are `queued|active|done|declined`, and
`queued` is the backlog — 46 tickets deep. Priority is the only sort inside it,
so a ticket that is genuinely important but deliberately not-now has nowhere to
go except a priority that lies about it.

Eric hit this on 2026-09-16 with six BadTakes tickets: BAD-041, BAD-042,
BAD-043 and BAD-048 (the four remaining file splits under the still-active
BAD-036) and BAD-040, all parked by choice; and BAD-021, which is waiting on
App Store approval — someone else's event, not a choice. Those four splits are
the **only** queued P1s in the whole ledger, so `spud board` leads with them
every session. Demoting them to P3 would have buried them among 28 others and
misstated their importance, so they were tagged instead: `deferred` on the five
parked by choice, `waiting` on BAD-021.

The tags are inert. Nothing reads them, so the board still opens with the four
splits and the tagging bought nothing until this ticket lands.

## What to decide

**Tag or status.** Tags were the cheap move that needed no schema change.
A fifth status (`deferred`) would make the state machine enforce it and would
show up in every rendered note and Bases view for free, at the cost of a
migration, new legal transitions, hook and render changes, and a decision about
what `waiting` then is. Settle this first and say why; the rest follows from it.

**What the board does by default.** Options, not a menu to implement:
hide parked tickets behind a flag (`--all`), sort them last regardless of
priority, or group them under their own heading. Whatever is chosen must also
hold for `spud board --brief`, which the `SessionStart` hook injects — that
injection is the surface that actually nags.

**Whether `waiting` differs from `deferred`.** Waiting on an external event
resolves on its own and is worth surfacing when it might have resolved;
deferred does not and is not.

## Scope

- `spud board` and `spud board --brief`, including what the `SessionStart` hook
  injects.
- `ledger/Board.base`: a view for the parked tickets, and excluding them from
  Board and By project. This ticket is the authority for that edit (CLAUDE.md
  allows a `.base` view only when a ticket specifies it).
- The schema, state machine, hooks and render only if the decision above lands
  on a status rather than a tag.

## Done when

The board no longer opens with a parked ticket; a parked ticket is still one
command away and is never silently lost; `spud board --help` documents how to
see them; Obsidian has a view for them; and the six tickets above read
correctly under whatever mechanism wins.

## Size, persona and model decision
One architect (fable) to settle tag-versus-status and what the board does by default, then one engineer (opus) for bin/spudlib plus the Board.base view. The architect question is the expensive-if-wrong half: a fifth status touches the schema, the state machine, the hooks and the render, and is hard to walk back.
